extracted.intended_audience: researchers of philanthropic foundations; Foundation Center staff; Council on Foundations staff; analysts of grantmaking to minority populations
extracted.subtask_short: analyzing foundation grant support to Hispanics
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology, classification rules, data-quality recommendations, and analytic dimensions for a study of foundation grantmaking benefiting Hispanics (1977-78), including how to identify, code, verify, and categorize grants and donees. Also includes policy recommendations to improve data and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise researchers on credibility measures
rubrics_metrics.description: When promoting research studies, the NCRP should advise researchers on necessary measures to insure credibility for each research study conducted on foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page recommends that researchers be advised on measures to ensure credibility; no detailed checklist is given here, but this functions as a high-level standard that studies on foundations should adopt explicit credibility safeguards (e.g., documentation, verification, transparent methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Council on Foundations support for survey response
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council on Foundations should engage in its own research and assist researchers in obtaining higher rates of response from foundations included in survey studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation that the Council proactively help increase foundation survey participation (e.g., outreach, endorsement, facilitation), as a way to improve data quality for foundation research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and correct Foundation Center codification system
rubrics_metrics.description: The system used by the Foundation Center staff for the codification and description of grants should be examined. Errors in the data banks must be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers and data stewards should audit coding systems, identify systematic errors, and correct database mistakes before analysis; implies periodic review of coding taxonomy and staff procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Foundation Grants Index (FGI) as data source
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers on foundation grant-making activities should be encouraged to use the Foundation Grants Index data base whenever possible, instead of using only IRS forms 990-AR, which offer extremely limited information. Also, FGI should not be an exclusive source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on data-source selection: prioritize FGI for richer information but corroborate with other sources (not exclusively rely on FGI); be aware of limits of IRS 990 forms for detailed grant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report transparency by foundations
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should be encouraged to include in their Annual Reports an informative description of the purposes of their grants and the names, addresses, and telephone numbers of donees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard for foundation reporting transparency to aid research and verification: include grant purpose narratives and contact details for recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundations’ role in verifying published listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the system used by the Foundation Center to code and describe listed grants is improved, foundations should collaborate in the quest for accuracy by examining the bi-monthly listing of grants made by the Foundation Center and published in Foundation News by the Council on Foundations. Foundations can then inform the Center of errors found in the listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical verification procedure: foundations regularly review published listings and report inaccuracies to the database maintainer to improve data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic classification dimensions for grant-support studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Support by foundations to Hispanics is examined under the following classifications: foundations acting as donors; groups designated as recipients; ethnicity of beneficiaries; Hispanic control of recipient boards of directors; geographic coverage of grants; fields of interest in which grants were awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These six dimensions form the core analytic framework for categorizing and reporting on grants in the study; analysts should collect and report metrics along each dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual search methodology using FGI
rubrics_metrics.description: The present study utilizes the [Foundation Grants Index] (for 1977 and 1978) on the basis of a manual search across 29,674 entries to identify and analyze grants which support Hispanics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological decision: a manual review of FGI entries was used to identify relevant grants; acknowledges tradeoffs between manual vs computerized searches (cost, need for repeated checking), and suggests manual search when necessary to capture nuanced categorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion criteria for grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants awarded to Hispanic or 'Spanish-speaking' organizations, or for the benefit of Hispanics living in the United States, excluding grants given to Puerto Ricans living in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, were extracted for further investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear geographic and beneficiary boundaries: include US-based Hispanic beneficiaries and Spanish-speaking organizations; explicitly exclude grants to Puerto Rico recipients living in Puerto Rico.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnicity classification categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The following categories were used to classify grants according to ethnicity: 1. Chicano - grants given to Mexican American recipients and/or for the benefit of Mexican American persons. 2. Puerto Ricans - grants given to Puerto Rican recipients in the United States, and/or for the benefit of Puerto Ricans in the U.S. 3. General Hispanic - grants given to Spanish and/or Hispanic recipients, not clearly Chicanos or Puerto Rican, to benefit 'Hispanics','the Spanish-speaking,' or 'Latinos.' 4. Mixed - grants given to benefit one or several Hispanic minorities and other non-Hispanic minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit category definitions when coding ethnicity of beneficiaries; allow for 'mixed' category where beneficiaries span multiple Hispanic groups and non-Hispanic minorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/regional grouping scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: The eighteen states in which grants were awarded for the benefit of Hispanics were grouped in the following regions: Northeast: Connecticut, Massachusetts, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, District of Columbia. North Central: Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio, Wisconsin, Nebraska. Southwest: Colorado, Arizona, California, Texas, New Mexico. Grants intended to benefit all regions were classified as 'national.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt and document a consistent regional grouping when analyzing geographic distribution; classify truly cross-region grants as 'national' and note any region-splitting conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data recording and multiple-order card sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants selected from the Index were recorded on note cards by a 'Hispanic recorder.' One card was prepared for each grant. With a second enumerator, the recorder checked the note cards against the Index for omissions, duplications, and errors. All grant cards were then photocopied in sets of different colors for a preliminary analysis, as follows: (White) - Alphabetically arranged by grantees; (Green) - Alphabetically arranged by foundations; (Peach) - Arranged by ethnicity of recipients; (Yellow) - Arranged by fields of interest in which grants were made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural QC: create one-record-per-grant, use independent second review, create multiple sorted copies to enable different analytic views and cross-check equality among sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spot checks and telephone verification
rubrics_metrics.description: While analyzing cards to categorize them in sets 3 and 4, inaccuracies were discovered in the Index entries. All such inaccuracies were corrected through telephone conversations or information provided by foundations. Although every grant could not be checked, spot checks were made to further reduce the number of inaccuracies that might remain undetected. Random telephone calls (to donees) for each assumption confirmed our hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data verification guidance: use telephone follow-ups with foundations and donees and perform spot checks to correct Index errors and validate classification assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification assumptions based on organization names and context
rubrics_metrics.description: The following assumptions were made when classifying grants: (a) All grants given to an agency having 'La Raza' as part of its legal title were considered Chicano, even if not specifically described as such in the grant purpose. (b) All grants given to agencies having a special reference to Puerto Rican history and culture as part of their legal names were likewise considered Puerto Rican. (c) Institutions thus assumed as Chicano or Puerto Rican were also assumed to be minority controlled. (d) Grants to provide 'bilingual,' 'bicultural' (or both), services in states and cities with a high concentration of Hispanic populations, or when Hispanics were the largest average ethnic minority, were assumed to be Spanish-English bilingual, and therefore related to the Hispanic population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rule-based heuristics for coding when grant descriptions are ambiguous; flag that such heuristics should be validated (authors used phone calls) and documented in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Hispanic-controlled' recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Of all grants to benefit Hispanics, 178 or 59% were allocated to agencies having at least 50% Hispanic representation on the Board of Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational definition: classify recipient agencies as Hispanic-controlled when at least 50% of board members are of Hispanic origin; use board composition as the control metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary analytic metrics for grant-support reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The study reports number of grants, total dollar value of grants, grants as percentage of all grants, number of foundations supporting Hispanics, average grant amounts for Hispanics and for all groups, percentage of grants allocated to Hispanic-controlled vs non-Hispanic-controlled agencies, and distribution of funds by ethnicity, field of interest, foundation, and region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing foundation support, collect and present counts, dollar totals, percentages of totals, averages, and cross-tabulations by donor, donee-ethnicity, donee-control status, field of interest, and geography; compare with prior studies when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for disproportionate influence of large donors/outliers
rubrics_metrics.description: Because The Ford Foundation contributed 54% of the total dollar value, the amount given by the remaining 94 foundations is reduced substantially; similarly, a single grant to ETS for $2,950,487 skews the 'Mixed' percentage as it accounts for more than half the monies in this category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic caveat: identify and, where appropriate, treat or report the influence of dominant donors and very large individual grants (e.g., present analyses with and without major donors/outliers to show their effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eight-field taxonomy for fields of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundation support for Hispanic needs and concerns can be separated into eight broad fields of interest: (a) Social Services - grants to agencies providing a wide variety of services to Hispanic individuals, youth, families and migrants, including bilingual/bicultural services and general support; (b) Community Organization and Development - grants to community agencies improving social/economic conditions through coalitions and citizen action (distinct from individual services); (c) Civil Rights and Legal Services - grants to MALDEF, PRLDEF, etc., covering litigation, voter registration, legal services, publications, education/internships; (d) Research - grants to support research activities directly relevant to Hispanics or a single Hispanic group; (e) Education - grants for educational leadership, scholarships, bilingual/bicultural education and language instruction, adult/remedial education and program improvement for Hispanics; (f) Health - physical and mental health services, training in health professions, general support for health services to Hispanics; (g) Arts and Humanities - grants supporting library collections, music instruction, performing arts, humanities conferences, Hispanic art exhibits, film development; (h) Religion - grants for concerted action of Hispanic churches, theological fellowships, conferences of Hispanic bishops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this eight-category taxonomy when coding field of interest for grants; include examples and recognize some projects may span categories (document primary purpose).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust regional percentages by excluding national-purpose funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Following HRC’s procedures, the percentages shown were adjusted by excluding funds given for national purposes. The adjusted percentages show better correspondence for some regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic practice: compute regional distributions both including and excluding national-purpose funds to assess correspondence with population distributions and to reduce distortion from nationally designated grants (e.g., fellowships).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report distributional summaries and frequency analyses of foundations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports include frequency of individual foundations supporting Hispanics by number of grants awarded (most foundations gave one or two grants), and ranking foundations and agencies by total dollar amounts and number of grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include frequency tables, histograms, and ranking tables to characterize donor behavior (e.g., counts of foundations giving 1-2 vs 3-4 vs 11+ grants) and to highlight concentration of support among a few donors/recipients.
